sessionName: Week 2 - Value proposition for operating partners
summary: Luke Badiali worked with Chris and Leanne on the value proposition built on the week 1 ICP of PE-backed manufacturers. We drafted a narrative around protecting the EBITDA bridge in the value-creation plan. The cost of inaction story and proof points need more work before they go into pitch materials.

discussion.keyPoints: Chris said operating partners judge them on EBITDA delivered against the investment case, not on lean maturity scores. Leanne agreed most pitch decks still lead with methodology.
There are good numbers from a recent packaging client (OEE up 14 points in 6 months) but client confidentiality limits naming. Chris is nervous about using any portfolio company name without consent.
Agreed the story should open with the gap between the investment case and actual plant performance, then show how Meridian closes it within the hold period.

recommendations.recommendation: Lead with: we deliver the operational EBITDA in your value-creation plan, typically £1m to £3m within 12 months per site.
Use a three-part story: investment case gap, 100-day mobilisation, measured EBITDA bridge, in every first meeting deck.
Build 4 anonymised proof cards, starting with the packaging client OEE gain of 14 points.
Quantify the cost of a 6-month delay in operational improvements as lost EBITDA multiplied by the exit multiple.

actions.action: Draft the four anonymised proof cards
Ask the packaging client for consent to quote the OEE result

nextFocus: Work out how Meridian generates demand beyond the three existing PE houses.
nextPreparation: Leanne to bring a list of all inbound enquiries and referral sources from the last 12 months.

tests.question: What value proposition did we agree to lead with?
Did we agree to use the cost of inaction calculation?
What was the plan for proof points?
